title: I Love Thy Zion, Lord
description: I Love Thy Zion, Lord in Tonic Solfa to AYLESBURY, doh is Ab: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 7 verses and a piano.
about: Timothy Dwight wrote these words. They were printed in the Evangelical Lutheran Hymn-Book (St. Louis, 1927), as hymn 468.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Short Metre (6.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to AYLESBURY; any other Short Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: I love Thy Zi-on, Lord, The house of Thine a-bode, The Church our blest Re-deem-er saved With His own pre-cious blood.

lines: The Church our blest Redeemer saved
I love Thy Church, O God!
Dear as the apple of Thine eye,
No! better far my tongue were dumb,
My hand its skill should lose.
For her my tears shall fall,
To her my cares and toils be given
Till toils and cares shall end.
Her hymns of love and praise.
Thy hand from every snare and foe
Sure as Thy truth shall last,
The brightest glories earth can yield

licence: Public domain: Timothy Dwight died in 1817.
credits: Words by Timothy Dwight (1752–1817), public domain, as printed in the Evangelical Lutheran Hymn-Book (1927); set to AYLESBURY by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
